clue.text: Black knight taken by English youth

indicators.note: the knight is taken in, captured, by the letters for English and youth together

parts.note: a youth is a boy
N is the chess notation for a knight

explanation.surface: A dark chess knight is captured by a young English player.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taken by' puts N inside E + BOY, between the O and the Y.
explanation.definitionFit: The name of a dense dark tropical hardwood is also used as a word for jet-black colour.

clue.text: House where they eat greens?

definitions.meaning: a house of Parliament, here the elected lower chamber at Westminster
shared village pastures where livestock graze, the greens being the grassy land itself

explanation.surface: A question about a home where vegetables are on the menu.
explanation.walkthrough: 'greens' looks like vegetables on a plate, but village greens are common land where animals graze.
explanation.definitionFit: The elected chamber of the UK Parliament is named after the common people, the same word used for shared grazing land.

clue.text: Baffle or drum might provide it?

definitions.meaning: to baffle someone is to stump or defeat them, as in 'it has me licked'
a drum supplies the rhythmic pulse of a piece of music

explanation.surface: Wondering whether a drum could supply sound-deadening material.
explanation.walkthrough: A baffle is also a sound-damping panel, which the surface leans on, but here it is a verb meaning to puzzle.
explanation.definitionFit: Puzzling someone is defeating them, and a drummer marks the rhythmic pulse of music: one word covers both senses.

clue.text: Potential politicians are frank over possible seat

parts.note: frank means candid, open and honest

indicators.note: possible signals that the word seat is only one possible arrangement of its letters

explanation.surface: Would-be MPs speak openly about a seat they might win.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over' is only a link: in a down clue the first piece sits above the second. 'possible' makes ATES from the seat letters.
explanation.definitionFit: People standing for election are hopefuls who may become politicians if they win.

clue.text: Do they help with gold braces?

parts.note: Au is the chemical symbol for gold
a brace is a pair, as in a brace of pheasants

explanation.surface: A question about whether people assist using golden fasteners.
explanation.walkthrough: 'braces' looks like trouser supports, but a brace is a couple of game birds, so braces are pairs.
explanation.definitionFit: Young foreign helpers live with a family and assist with childcare and housework.

clue.text: A long time to answer good points

parts.note: E and S, east and south, are points of the compass

explanation.surface: It takes ages to answer the questions on good points.
explanation.walkthrough: 'points' gives two compass points, E and S.
explanation.definitionFit: An eternity or a very lengthy period, as in waiting forever for a bus.

clue.text: A gun in America means tranquillity, say

indicators.note: say signals that the word for tranquillity is heard, giving a different spelling

parts.note: tranquillity is peace, calm and quiet

explanation.surface: An American firearm is said to stand for calm, an ironic claim.
explanation.definitionFit: In US slang a handgun is called by this word, as in 'packing heat'.

clue.text: Take off and put it in individual team display

parts.note: I, the Roman numeral one, stands for an individual

indicators.note: put it in tells us the two letters go inside the rearranged team
display suggests the letters of team are shown in a new arrangement

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A performer removes something and slots it into a team exhibition.
explanation.walkthrough: 'display' reworks the team letters as MATE; 'Take off' reads as removing, but means mimic.
explanation.definitionFit: To take off someone is to mimic or impersonate them for comic effect.

clue.text: Observer features a Prescott blunder!

indicators.note: a blunder is a mistake, so the letters are muddled up

explanation.surface: A newspaper reporting a gaffe by John Prescott, the former Labour deputy prime minister.
explanation.walkthrough: John Prescott was a British Labour deputy prime minister famous for verbal gaffes; 'blunder' rearranges A PRESCOTT. The Observer is also a British Sunday paper.
explanation.definitionFit: A watcher at a match or show is an onlooker, someone who views rather than takes part.

clue.text: Joey called — said he'd come back!

definitions.text: Joey called — said he'd come back!

parts.words: Joey called — said he'd come back!
parts.note: a joey is a baby kangaroo, so this is an Australian thing that famously returns after it is thrown

explanation.surface: A man named Joey phoned and promised to return.
explanation.walkthrough: Joey reads as a person's name, but a joey is a young kangaroo, pointing to Australia, home of the curved hunting stick that returns.
explanation.definitionFit: An Australian curved throwing stick is designed to fly back to the thrower.

clue.text: One in isolation just returned before it started easing

indicators.note: returned says the word for just goes back the way it came

parts.note: just means mere, as in a mere child
taken as written

indicators.note: started points to the letter the word easing starts with

explanation.surface: A recluse just came back before things started to get easier.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returned' turns MERE into EREM; 'started' takes E from easing.
explanation.definitionFit: A hermit lives alone in a remote place, often for religious reasons.

clue.text: Tom needs a fix! He's got worms

indicators.note: a fix is a setting right, so these letters are rearranged into new order

explanation.surface: Tom needs medication because he has parasites.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fix' reads as a dose or a cure, but it rearranges TOM NEEDS A.
explanation.definitionFit: Roundworms form a large phylum of slender unsegmented creatures, many of them parasites.

clue.text: The eastern Mediterranean is allowed to import commercial transport

indicators.note: to import is to bring in, so one word goes inside the other

parts.note: something allowed is let, as in 'let go'
a van is a commercial vehicle for goods

explanation.surface: Trade in the eastern Mediterranean may bring in delivery vehicles.
explanation.definitionFit: An old name for the lands of the eastern Mediterranean coast, from the French for rising, as in sunrise.

clue.text: Independent former wife makes a list

parts.note: an ex is a former spouse

explanation.surface: A divorced woman of independent means draws up a list.
explanation.definitionFit: An alphabetical catalogue of topics at the back of a book is a list.

clue.text: Native regularly catching giant crab

indicators.note: regularly means taking every other letter, here the second, fourth and so on

explanation.surface: A local person routinely catches an enormous crab.
explanation.walkthrough: 'catching' is a link here; 'regularly' takes the even letters of GIANT CRAB.
explanation.definitionFit: A member of the indigenous people of the Andes, whose empire ruled Peru before the Spanish conquest.

clue.text: Fear finding one in a phone box out of order?

indicators.note: out of order means not in proper sequence, a nod to a broken phone box, so the letters are scrambled

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Being frightened when finding someone inside a broken phone box.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out of order' suggests a broken phone, but rearranges I + A PHONE BOX.
explanation.definitionFit: Dread or hatred of foreigners and strangers is a specific fear.

clue.text: Animal that consequently gets stuck into a wine container

indicators.note: gets stuck into puts one word inside the other

parts.note: a bin is a rack or store for wine bottles
so means therefore or consequently

explanation.surface: Something that ends up jammed in a wine rack.
explanation.definitionFit: The large shaggy wild ox of North America is a beast of the plains.

clue.text: Meals on wheels training?

parts.note: food served on a railway carriage that rolls on wheels, with training read as going by train

explanation.surface: Instruction for volunteers who deliver meals to elderly people.
explanation.walkthrough: Meals on wheels is a British service delivering hot food to the housebound; 'training' here means travelling by rail.
explanation.definitionFit: A railway coach where passengers buy food is quite literally meals on wheels.

clue.text: Resent a criminal being sincere

indicators.note: criminal means wrong or crooked, so the letters are bent out of order

explanation.surface: Someone resents a lawbreaker who seems genuine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'criminal' looks like a noun but rearranges RESENT A.
explanation.definitionFit: A heartfelt, serious person is sincere and genuine.

clue.text: Free to cover a sudden attack

indicators.note: to cover is to go around something, so one word wraps the other

parts.note: to free of something is to rid it

explanation.surface: Release someone in order to shield them from an assault.
explanation.definitionFit: A swift surprise assault, as by police or troops, is a strike.

clue.text: Very small (3/4) container

indicators.note: three quarters means keeping three of the four letters of the word for very small

parts.note: very small means tiny

explanation.surface: A tiny receptacle is marked with a fraction.
explanation.walkthrough: The '(3/4)' tells you to keep three quarters of TINY, dropping the Y.
explanation.definitionFit: A metal can holds food or paint.

clue.text: Oddly forbid access to ship

indicators.note: Oddly means taking the odd letters, first third and fifth

parts.note: a gate gives access

explanation.surface: Strangely, banning entry to a vessel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Oddly' reads as strangely, but takes F, R, I from forbid.
explanation.definitionFit: A medium-sized warship, once a sailing ship and now an escort vessel.

clue.text: Bury's got one motorway (provisional)

parts.note: to bury is to inter
I is the Roman numeral one
M stands for motorway, as in the M1

explanation.surface: Bury, a Lancashire town, has a temporary motorway.
explanation.walkthrough: Bury reads as the Lancashire town, but it is the verb to bury. M is the British prefix for motorways.
explanation.definitionFit: An arrangement meant to last only until a permanent one is made is a stopgap.

clue.text: Part of a rich orange vein?

indicators.note: Part of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A deep orange streak running through something.
explanation.walkthrough: The '?' warns that 'vein' is loose: the definition is what flowed in the veins of the Greek gods.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth an ethereal fluid flowed through the gods' veins in place of blood.

clue.text: Workers working with practical experience

parts.note: hands are workers, as in farmhands
on means working, as in 'the machine is on'

explanation.surface: Labourers on the job know what they are doing.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who has done the job directly, rather than in theory, is practically involved.

clue.text: Plant juice? — I would find it tasty

parts.note: sap is the fluid that circulates in plants
I'd is short for I would

explanation.surface: Asking whether the juice of a plant would taste good.
explanation.definitionFit: A rare word for something with a pleasant flavour, the opposite of insipid.

clue.text: Access given to the course?

definitions.meaning: access means right of entry or admission
a course of a meal, in Britain the one before the main dish and in America the main dish itself

explanation.surface: Entry is granted to the racecourse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'course' suggests a golf or race course but means a dish in a meal.
explanation.definitionFit: Admission into a place, and also a dish served at dinner: one word covers both.

clue.text: Dash in front of last wild animal

parts.note: dash means flair or panache, élan

indicators.note: last points to the final letter of the word wild

explanation.surface: Rushing ahead of the final wild creature.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dash' looks like a verb meaning rush, but is the noun meaning style.
explanation.definitionFit: A large African antelope with spiral horns is a wild beast.

clue.text: A way to accept national guard with anxiety

indicators.note: to accept is to take in, so the first letters go around the second

parts.note: St is the abbreviation for street, a way
NG is the abbreviation for National Guard

explanation.surface: A path that lets in a national guard is fraught with worry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to accept' sets the guard letters after the A. The National Guard is a US reserve military force.
explanation.definitionFit: A German-derived word for deep dread or existential worry.

clue.text: Possessed and working after father disapproved!

indicators.note: after means the possessed and working pieces follow the letters for father

parts.note: Fr is the abbreviation for Father, a priest's title
possessed means owned
on means working, operating

explanation.surface: A dad disapproved of someone who is possessed and at work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Possessed' suggests demonic possession, but means owned.
explanation.definitionFit: Looking down on something with a scowl means disapproving of it.

clue.text: Charge student for experience

parts.note: a fee is a charge for a service
L is for learner, as on a British learner driver's plate

explanation.surface: Charging a student for some life experience.
explanation.walkthrough: L stands for learner, from the L-plates on British learner drivers' cars.
explanation.definitionFit: To undergo a sensation or emotion is to sense it.

clue.text: The issue turns to hotel food

indicators.note: turns means the word for issue is turned back to front

parts.note: a son is issue, offspring
H is hotel in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: The child turns to the hotel for a meal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'issue' means offspring, giving SON; 'turns' makes NOS.
explanation.definitionFit: British slang for grub, informal eating.

clue.text: Flowers carried in mixed cargoes

indicators.note: mixed means the letters of cargoes are jumbled together

explanation.surface: Blooms are transported in assorted shipments.
explanation.definitionFit: A small spray of blooms worn pinned to a dress or wrist.

clue.text: Spain has undertakings on discharges

parts.note: E is the international vehicle code for Spain (España)
missions are undertakings or assignments

explanation.surface: Spain takes on projects concerning pollution.
explanation.definitionFit: Gases or fluids released into the air are outflows.

clue.text: Engineers' template gets makeover

parts.note: RE stands for the Royal Engineers, a British Army corps
a model is a template or pattern to copy

explanation.surface: The engineering corps' blueprint is overhauled.
explanation.walkthrough: RE is the Royal Engineers, a corps of the British Army.
explanation.definitionFit: To reshape or renovate something is to give it a new form.
